course_name_original: I.C. SIGNAL ANALYSIS AND STATISTICAL METHODS FOR BIOENGINEERING
course_name_en: Integrated Course: Signal Analysis and Statistical Methods for Bioengineering
prerequisites: Knowledge of elements of physiology, analysis and physics
Knowledge of rudiments of Matlab coding
Functions of two or more variables

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the theoretical and methodological foundations for analyzing biomedical signals in the time, frequency, and time-frequency domains, with particular emphasis on: physiological signal acquisition and digitization; filtering and preprocessing; spectral analysis; feature extraction for diagnosis and monitoring; an introduction to the analysis of non-stationary signals.
Interpret results from a physiological perspective.
Implement simple algorithms in MATLAB or Python.
Understand notions of probability theory and mathematical statistics for the management of uncertainty and for making predictions.

syllabus_topics: Biomedical Signals (Classification, Continuous and Discrete Signals, Acquisition, Types)
Sampling and the Nyquist-Shannon Theorem
Quantization and Noise
Applications of Biomedical Signals: ECG, EMG, EEG, PPG, fNIRS
Time Domain Analysis: Statistical Parameters (Mean, Variance, RMS), Autocorrelation, Cross-Correlation, Convolution, Impulse Response of LTI Systems
Analysis of RR variability in the ECG
Frequency Analysis: Fourier Series and Transform, DFT and FFT, Power Spectral Density (PSD)
Physiological Spectral Interpretation (EEG Bands, EMG Spectrum, Respiratory Analysis)
Digital Filtering: FIR and IIR Filters, Low-pass, high-pass, and notch filter design
Network Noise Removal (50 Hz)
Adaptive Filtering (basic information)
ECG Signal Cleaning
Time-Frequency Analysis: STFT and Spectrogram, Introduction to Wavelets, Non-stationary Signals
Applications to Dynamic EEG and EMG
Feature Extraction and Introduction to Pattern Recognition: Feature Extraction in Time and Frequency
Dimensionality Reduction (PCA, ICA)
Introduction to Supervised Classification (basics)
Connection to Medical Devices and AI
Laboratory Activities: MATLAB Exercises (Sampling Simulation, FFT and PSD Calculation, Digital Filter Design, Spectrogram Analysis)
Probability Theory: Events, Probability, Total Probability Theorem, Conditional Probability, Combinatorics
Independence (Logical and Stochastic), Bayes Theorem, Bayesian Networks
Random Variables: Expectation, Moments, Distribution Function, Moment Generating Function
Discrete Distributions: Binomial, Geometric, Poisson
Continuous Distributions: Uniform, Exponential, Gaussian, Gamma, Lognormal
Law of Large Numbers
Central Limit Theorem
Statistical Inference

assessment_methods.method: Written test (multiple-choice, open-ended questions, problem-solving) for Signal Analysis module
First written test for Statistics and Probability Methods module
Second written test for Statistics and Probability Methods module
Oral examination for Statistics and Probability Methods module

assessment_rules: For the Signal Analysis module, the final written test is graded on a scale of 18-30, with honors awarded for correctly answering all questions. For the Statistics and Probability Methods module, the final grade is the arithmetic mean of two written tests and one oral examination. Students not taking periodic assessments for the Statistics module will have one written test and one oral examination. The minimum passing grade is 18/30. The syllabus does not provide specific resit arrangements.
